extracted.intended_audience: business and finance news readers; investors, corporate communicators, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A news article reporting SEC charges against corporate executives for misleading investors about key performance metrics; demonstrates regulatory expectations for investor communications and possible enforcement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of executive statements about key performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: "If executives speak about a key performance metric to promote their business, they must do so fully and accurately," said Stephanie Avakian, director of the SEC's Division of Enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When executives publicly discuss metrics used to promote the company, those statements must be complete and accurate. Anti-patterns include promoting a metric while omitting known problems that materially change its meaning or reliability. Enforcement risk arises when statements are knowingly misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability for certified investor disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The two executives had certified in 2015 and 2016 investor disclosures that touted the firm's supposedly robust "cross-sell" metric, despite knowing it was misleading, the SEC said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executives who certify investor disclosures can be held responsible if the certified statements are misleading. Claiming that statements were vetted by internal policies or others may be contested but does not necessarily shield certifiers from enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on endorsing inflated or misleading metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolstedt publicly endorsed the firm's vaunted cross-sell metric from 2014 through 2016, despite the fact that it was "inflated by accounts and services that were unused, unneeded, or unauthorized."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not endorse or publicize performance metrics that are inflated by improper practices (e.g., unauthorized accounts, unused services). Practical guidance: verify that metrics reflect legitimate, authorized customer activity and that reporting systems and controls prevent artificial inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement consequences for misleading investors
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC's complaint ... charges Tolstedt with fraud and seeks penalties and to ban her from being an officer or director of a public company. Stumpf agreed to pay a $2.5 million civil penalty to resolve the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory remedies for misleading investor communications can include civil fraud charges, monetary penalties, and officer/director bars. Examples from the article: a $2.5M civil penalty for an individual and requests for bans on serving as an officer or director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlements and restitution to investors
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier this year, Wells Fargo paid $3 billion to settle several U.S. probes into its operations... The regulator said it will distribute money collected from Stumpf and the bank to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement resolutions may include large corporate settlements and the distribution of collected funds to harmed investors. Press communications and disclosures around settlements should accurately reflect the nature of the remedies and any restitution processes.
